newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close lower on weaker cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close lower on weaker cash ideas.

text.p: Expectations cash cattle prices will soon recede weighed on CME live cattle futures much of the day and finally pushed them to a lower close. Feeder cattle closed mixed on spillover selling from live cattle, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.575 to 0.075 cent per lb lower with August off most at 63.375 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.275 lower to 0.150 higher with August off 0.175 at 78.300 cents.
Renewed concern that cash markets will trend lower, partly due to seasonal considerations, perpetuated commercial selling in live cattle futures until late in the session, traders said.
Boxed beef values slipped at noon amid talk that demand for beef is usually light after buying for Independence Day features wanes.
USDA quoted beef cut-out values down $0.29 to $0.46 per cwt at midday.
Fed cattle supplies will also be large which should keep cash prices pressured into the fall, sources noted.
Refco, R.J. O'Brien, Cargill Investor Services and Dean Witter sold into sell stops before scattered short covering developed at the closing bell, traders said.
Lind-Waldock spread long February/short June 1998 early, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, a commercial sold the October 66 synthetic put, selling calls and buying futures. Commercials sold August 64 calls. Commission houses sold August 62 puts late. Volatility was steady to weak, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures traded choppy and weakened again shortly before the close on a break in live cattle futures and higher CBOT corn futures. Feeders had rallied for gains around midsession, buoyed by reports of strong cash feeder markets, traders said.
In addition to a seasonal slip in cash fed cattle prices mid- to late summer, there also is a strong seasonal tendency for feeders to rally this time of year, some sources noted.
However, the latest CME feeder cattle index fell $0.45 per cwt to $77.56.

Cargill Investor Services notably bought August early while E.D.&F. Man sold. Locals bought while Lind-Waldock spread long April live cattle/short August feeder cattle. Cargill and ING bought September, pit sources said.
